name: stats
description: Statistics for AQL: descriptive, inferential, and matrix statistics exposed as the single `Stats` namespace, plus a streaming `Summary` accumulator. Descriptive words accept a List of numbers or a Summary; order statistics take a List only; the dataset words operate on an aql:matrix-util Matrix.

conventions.import: import "./stats.aql"  — no `end` needed; the library imports its own aql:* deps (math-util, array-util, matrix-util, struct-util). Callers who BUILD a Matrix to pass to the dataset words must `import "aql:matrix-util"` themselves — the MatrixUtil binding is not re-exported.
conventions.call: verb-first, all-forward: `Stats.verb data arg... end` (the verb, then the data, then any extra args, terminated with `end` or wrapped in parens). Without a terminator the verb swallows the following token, giving a wrong result or a dispatch error. (The core words each/fold, indexing `get`, and the matrix accessors MatrixUtil.row/col read their subject from the stack and stay subject-first.)
conventions.input_polymorphism: every descriptive word (mean, sum, count, min, max, range, variance, pvariance, stddev, pstddev, skewness, kurtosis) accepts EITHER a List of numbers OR a Summary; the order-statistic words (median, quantile, iqr, mode) require the raw data and take a List only (a Summary raises needs_data).
conventions.sample_vs_population: the unqualified `variance`/`stddev` are SAMPLE statistics (divide by n-1); `pvariance`/`pstddev` are POPULATION (divide by n). Likewise `covariance` is sample, `pcovariance` is population.
conventions.numeric: inputs may be Integer or Float; results are Float (count is Integer). All arithmetic is done in Float — Integer overflow is a hard error in aql, not a silent wrap.
conventions.mutation: summary/push/push-all/merge MUTATE the receiver Summary in place and return the SAME object — there is no immutable copy.
conventions.matrix_layout: the dataset words take a Matrix whose ROWS are observations and COLUMNS are variables. Per-column statistics return a List; cov-matrix/cor-matrix/standardize return a Matrix.
conventions.ols: Stats.ols takes a design Matrix X (rows = observations, cols = predictors) and a response List y, and returns the least-squares coefficients via the normal equations (XᵀX b = Xᵀy), solved by Gaussian elimination with partial pivoting. Prepend a column of 1s to X for an intercept term.
conventions.import_resolution: relative to the working directory the script is run from, not the importing file
conventions.errors: failures raise coded errors caught with `do [...] error [...]`; read e.code / e.message. Codes: bad_input (empty/too-few data, quantile q outside [0,1], non-positive sigma, mismatched vector lengths), needs_data (an order-statistic / bivariate word called on a Summary), singular (Stats.ols normal equations have no unique solution), bad_payload (Stats.decode text is not a Stats.encode snapshot)
conventions.serialization: encode produces a jsonic snapshot of a Summary's moments (n, mean, m2, m3, m4, min, max); decode rebuilds an equivalent Summary. Whole-valued Floats render without a decimal point, so decode coerces field types back.

Summary.note: sealed class of running central moments (Welford/Pébay); construct only via Stats.summary; fields are read-only. m2/m3/m4 are the central-moment sums Σ(x-mean)^k.

summary.note: Build a streaming accumulator from a List of numbers ([] gives an empty Summary).

push.note: MUTATES s, returns the SAME object. Welford update.

push-all.note: MUTATES s with every element of xs, returns it.

merge.note: Combine the moments of b into a (parallel/Pébay combine). MUTATES a and returns it. Always compatible (no parameters to disagree on). O(1).

encode.note: jsonic snapshot of the moments. Round-trips through Stats.decode.

decode.note: Rebuild a Summary from a snapshot. Raises bad_payload on unparseable or incomplete text.

skewness.note: Biased sample skewness g1 = (m3/n)/(m2/n)^1.5. Raises bad_input on zero-variance data.

kurtosis.note: Biased excess kurtosis g2 = (m4/n)/(m2/n)^2 - 3. Raises bad_input on zero-variance data.

median.note: List only (needs raw data; a Summary raises needs_data).

quantile.note: q in [0,1], linear interpolation (NumPy/R type-7). q out of range raises bad_input. List only.

iqr.note: Inter-quartile range Q3 - Q1. List only.

mode.note: Most frequent value; on a tie, the smallest such value. List only.

covariance.note: SAMPLE covariance. Needs >= 2 paired values; mismatched lengths raise bad_input.

correlation.note: Pearson correlation coefficient r in [-1, 1]. Undefined (bad_input) if a variable has zero variance.

linreg.note: Simple linear regression of ys on xs. Returns {slope, intercept, r, r2}. Predictor must have non-zero variance.

zscores.note: Sample-standardised values (x - mean)/stddev. Zero stddev raises bad_input.

normal-pdf.note: Normal probability density at x. sigma > 0 (else bad_input).

normal-cdf.note: Normal cumulative probability at x, via an Abramowitz-Stegun erf approximation (abs error ~1.5e-7). sigma > 0.

cov-matrix.note: SAMPLE covariance matrix (1/(n-1)) XcᵀXc. Needs >= 2 rows.

ols.note: Least-squares coefficients via XᵀX b = Xᵀy. Rows of X must match length of y; a rank-deficient system raises singular. Prepend a 1s column for an intercept.
